title: S1 V3.9 + S2 V3.2 — the two strategies as a portfolio, not as two strategies
strategy: S1 AweWithBB V3.9; S2 Hammer V3.2 — portfolio construction
question: After a bar-level alpha search found nothing tradeable, is there anything left in how the two existing strategies are combined — and can a genuinely uncorrelated third strategy be found for the same instrument, long or short?
hypothesis: Expected close to nothing. Two long-only strategies on the same instrument should be near-redundant, and a diversification claim between them looked like a relabelling of the same directional bet.

findings.title: The two strategies are much less redundant than they look
findings.detail: Monthly R returns correlate at 0.234 (Pearson) and 0.344 (Spearman) across 32 months, with both trading in 29 of them. Two long-only strategies on the same instrument were expected to be near-duplicates; they are not, and that is the whole basis for anything else here.

findings.title: Blending is strongly better than running S2 alone
findings.detail: A 50/50 risk split lifts the annualised Sharpe from 2.327 to 3.882 and cuts the worst drawdown from 12.79R to 2.17R. Resampling months gives P(improvement > 0) = 0.999 for Sharpe and 0.99 for drawdown, with a 90% interval of [0.763, 2.377] on the Sharpe gain.

findings.title: And it is NOT demonstrably better than running S1 alone
findings.detail: Against S1 the Sharpe gain is 0.218 with a 90% interval of [-0.753, 0.985] and P(>0) = 0.649. That interval crosses zero comfortably. Reporting only the S2 comparison would have turned a real but one-sided result into a recommendation the data does not carry.

findings.title: The weight does not matter, which is the useful part
findings.detail: Sharpe runs from 3.707 to 3.958 across every S1 weight between 0.4 and 0.8. The in-sample optimum sits inside that plateau, so it carries no information. 50/50 is reported because it is the weight a person picks without looking, and it gives up almost nothing.

findings.title: The Sharpe level is not a live expectation and the comparison is
findings.detail: Values near 3.9 do not survive real execution. These are Strategy Tester R multiples aggregated monthly over a market that rose 112%, with no slippage beyond the export's own. Every claim here is a ranking between allocations of the same backtest, never a forecast of what either will return.

findings.title: Per year the blend leads twice out of three
findings.detail: The 50/50 blend has the best Sharpe of the three options in 2/3 years. In 2026 S1 alone is better, because S2 had a weak year — which is what a diversification result should look like rather than a uniform win.

findings.title: The strategies are mostly alpha, so an uncorrelated third is not structurally blocked
findings.detail: Regressing monthly R on gold's monthly return gives S1 a beta of 0.444 and S2 0.27, with R-squared of 0.22 and 0.116. 79.7% of S1's return and 77.0% of S2's is alpha rather than being long gold, and in the 8 months gold fell both were still positive (4.06R and 1.507R). Had they been mostly beta, decorrelating would have required shorting gold and the search would have been hopeless. Caveat: this is backtest alpha, and the version history from V3.4 to V4.1 is itself a selection process.

findings.title: A counter-trend fade is genuinely uncorrelated and genuinely unprofitable
findings.detail: Fading a two-bar move of 2.5 ATR, held 8 bars, is symmetric long and short and correlates 0.036 with the blend, -0.054 with S1 and 0.128 with S2 — exactly the property being looked for. Over 700 trades its own Sharpe is -0.046 and its total is -3.08R, so it lowers the blend's Sharpe at every weight tested (3.882 down to 2.911 at 30%). Two of four variants held their sign from train to valid; surviving that is not the same as being worth adding.

findings.title: The structural mirror of S2 does not work as a short
findings.detail: S2's hammer definition was reverse-engineered from the export's own flags and each characteristic reflected — body, both wicks, close position and Bollinger position — giving 96 shooting-star signals against 212 hammers. Shorting them loses in every period and every exit rule tested, with win rates from 13% to 39%. A working long pattern does not become a working short by reflection.

findings.title: The reusable output is the bar a new strategy has to clear
findings.detail: At a 30% risk allocation, a candidate needs a Sharpe of 0.8 to improve the blend if it is uncorrelated, 1.65 at correlation 0.25 and 2.44 at 0.50 — but only -0.14 at correlation −0.25, where a candidate helps while losing money slightly. Correlation is worth more than return, which argues for a different instrument rather than another rule on this one.

card_summary: S1 and S2 as one portfolio: correlation 0.234, and what that is worth.
